properties.rationale: Standing disposition for planned-but-unbuilt capabilities. The check divides as the capability does, and the cheap half is genuinely cheap: the conjunction scan and the single-owner rule are deterministic and get ordinary fixture tests ("must do X AND Y" is flagged; a leaf whose satisfying capabilities allocate to three components is flagged). The over-decomposition half cannot be unit-tested for correctness — a test asserting the fixture was flagged only proves the fixture was flagged — so what must be pinned there is that a complaint about grain never edits or splits anything, only asks. Worth building the conjunction scan first regardless: it is a text check needing no model, it catches the commonest compound requirement, and it would have something to say about real designs on day one.
